author: Rahul kp
title: Economic Order
simple_words: EOQ is the order size where ordering cost and carrying cost for the year are lowest together.

definitions.meaning: The ==order quantity== that minimises the total of annual ordering cost and annual carrying cost of inventory.
definitions.note: At EOQ, ordering cost = carrying cost

definitions.meaning: Cost of holding stock: storage, insurance, obsolescence, interest on funds blocked. Stated per unit per year.
definitions.note: Convert % to ₹ per unit per year

key_points: Total ordering cost for the year rises when orders are many (small order size)
Total carrying cost (Q/2 × C) rises when the order size is big
Cost per order (O) stays the same whatever the order size
At EOQ, total ordering cost equals total carrying cost
formula_hook: one root, C at the bottom

formulas.name: Economic Order Quantity
formulas.legend: A = annual demand (units); O = cost per order (₹); C = carrying cost per unit per year (₹)

formulas.name: Total annual ordering cost
formulas.legend: Q = order quantity (units); A/Q = number of orders in the year

formulas.name: Total annual carrying cost
formulas.legend: Q/2 = average stock held, assuming uniform usage and no safety stock

insight.punchline: Many small orders or few big ones?
insight.text: EOQ balances the two: more orders cut carrying cost but raise ordering cost, and the reverse.

memory_trick.explanation: Top of the fraction: 2, A, O multiplied. Carrying cost C is the divisor at the bottom. Put the whole fraction under one square root.

steps: Find A in units per year
Make C ₹ per unit per year
exam_tip: If carrying cost is given as a % of unit price, first multiply it by price to get C in ₹ per unit per year.

doubt.question: Why is carrying cost Q/2 and not Q?
doubt.answer: Stock falls from Q to zero before the next lot arrives, so the average stock held is Q/2, assuming uniform usage.

mistakes.wrong: Using monthly demand as A with a yearly C
mistakes.right: Keep A and C on the same period: annual demand and carrying cost per unit per year.

mistakes.wrong: Putting C in % of price directly in the formula
mistakes.right: Convert it first: C = % × price per unit, in ₹ per unit per year.
EOQ = √(2AO / C): carrying cost is the divisor.

mistakes.wrong: Saying EOQ is where total cost is highest
mistakes.right: EOQ is where total of ordering and carrying cost is lowest.

reviewer_note: Fixed key point 1 and mnemonic. EOQ assumes uniform usage, no stock-outs, constant prices.
check_notes: Writer: Fixed key point 1 and mnemonic. EOQ assumes uniform usage, no stock-outs, constant prices.

Checker 1: simple_words: 'where ordering cost and carrying cost for the year are lowest together' can be read as saying each cost is at its own lowest. In fact ordering cost keeps falling and carrying cost keeps rising as the order size grows. Better: 'EOQ is the order size at which the total of annual ordering cost and annual carrying cost is lowest.'
